record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/npcc.pdf). Version 1.1; no date of the version itself is printed, only the endorsement date (28 Sep 2023). Whether a later version of the Covenant exists was not checked. Principle B3 is truncated in the source PDF itself (item (1) ends with ';' and no item (2) follows). Binding=false (not law); members endorsed it and 'all developers and users of AI within policing must give due regard' to its principles, recorded as status 'enforceable' with that weaker 'due regard' qualifier. Several principles use 'will'/'should'; modality reflects the stated wording.

clauses.original_text: Principle B. Transparent: All use of AI will be subject to ‘Maximum Transparency by Default’ (MTbD). B1. Forces should ensure the public are aware of AI uses. This will typically include publishing an overview of the algorithms used and the known limitations of the training data used.
clauses.object: AI uses, algorithms and training-data limitations
clauses.requirement: publish overview of algorithms and known training-data limitations
clauses.exception: B2: where operational or security requirements restrict sharing, independent assessors scrutinise instead
clauses.applicable_systems: AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics used in policing

clauses.original_text: Principle C. Explainable: The ability for any AI to provide an ‘explanation’ of its output will be a determining factor in its implementation.
clauses.requirement: explainability determines whether AI is implemented
clauses.applicable_systems: AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics used in policing
clauses.interpretation_notes: Phrased with 'will'; C1 scales the expected explanation to the function (e.g. high-impact decisions about individuals) and audience.

clauses.original_text: Principle D. Responsible: All AI that affects the public will have responsible usage policies (i.e., intensions are defined before deployment so that outcomes and impact can be tracked) and procedures to ensure that users do not accept AI outputs uncritically. … D2. All AI that effects the public must have a human as the ultimate decision-maker.
clauses.action: keep a human as ultimate decision-maker; prevent uncritical acceptance
clauses.requirement: human ultimate decision-maker; usage policies against uncritical acceptance of outputs
clauses.affected_asset: rights of members of the public
clauses.applicable_systems: AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics used in policing

clauses.original_text: D3. All AI will have a human or automatic means of being stopped if it displays unintended or undesired outputs.
clauses.requirement: human or automatic means to stop AI
clauses.condition: AI displays unintended or undesired outputs
clauses.applicable_systems: AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics used in policing

clauses.original_text: D4. Those responsible for AI-enabled systems must proactively mitigate the risk of unintended biases or harms, during initial rollout and as they learn, change, or are redeployed.
clauses.requirement: proactive bias/harm mitigation across the lifecycle
clauses.condition: at rollout and as systems learn, change or are redeployed
clauses.applicable_systems: AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics used in policing
clauses.interpretation_notes: F2 adds a force data framework to guard against bias, unintended proxies, non-representativeness, unfairness and untimeliness.

clauses.original_text: Principle F. Robust: All data used to train, or that is analysed by, an AI will be robust and reliable enough for its intended purpose. … F1. All AI in policing will be used only for the purpose it was designed, trained and authorised for.
clauses.action: ensure data quality; limit use to authorised purpose
clauses.requirement: robust, reliable data; use only for designed, trained and authorised purpose
clauses.purpose: reliable analysis and avoidance of misuse
clauses.applicable_systems: AI, machine learning and advanced data analytics used in policing
clauses.interpretation_notes: Phrased with 'will'; requires assessing, tracking and reporting on data quality.
